title: Brown refinement mates are invertible and compose
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a normed finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a field $k$ whose characteristic is prime and different from $\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$, and a specified normalized compact-support comparison family $C$ [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Use the actual functors, maps, supplied pairs, and normalized Brown data of [def-pur-reconstructed-refinement-data]. For a refinement $w:c\to d$, normalized Brown packages $D_1,D_2$, an integral object $L$ on $Y$, and supplied systems $A_1,A_2$ over $L$, the actual Brown mate $\rho_{12}:D_2.\operatorname{output}(L)\to D_1.\operatorname{output}(L)$ is invertible. It is defined by the inverse of the first transported Hom bijection applied to the forward system comparison followed by the second counit. For composable refinements $r:c\to d$, $s:d\to e$ and three such packages and supplied systems, $\rho_{13}(s\circ r)=\rho_{12}(r)\circ\rho_{23}(s)$. These are equations of actual system maps, with no reconstructed or scalar trace conclusion.

proof.text:
the Brown Hom formula sends each defined mate to its prescribed system
comparison followed by the second counit. Define the reverse arrow by transposing
the inverse system comparison followed by the first counit under the second Hom
bijection. Both outputs lie in the common intrinsic origin domain. Naturality of
the system comparison and the two counit equations show that each composite has
the same transpose as the identity. Injectivity of the Brown Hom bijections proves
they are inverse. For three compactifications transpose the composite of mates;
use both counit equations, naturality, and composition of the intrinsic refinement
maps conjugated by beta. The resulting transpose is that of the direct mate, so
injectivity proves composition. These are equations of system maps.

lean.statement:
theorem reconstructedBrownMateLaws :
    (∀ (c d : Compactification f)
    (D₁ : At l E k C X Y f c) (D₂ : At l E k C X Y f d) (w : c.Refinement d)
    (L : CondensedERealization.Integral l E Y.scheme)
    (A₁ : D₁.Supplied L) (A₂ : D₂.Supplied L), IsIso (mate D₁ D₂ w L A₁ A₂)) ∧
    (∀ (c d e : Compactification f)
    (D₁ : At l E k C X Y f c) (D₂ : At l E k C X Y f d) (D₃ : At l E k C X Y f e)
    (r : c.Refinement d) (s : d.Refinement e)
    (L : CondensedERealization.Integral l E Y.scheme)
    (A₁ : D₁.Supplied L) (A₂ : D₂.Supplied L) (A₃ : D₃.Supplied L),
    mate D₁ D₃ (r.comp s) L A₁ A₃ = mate D₂ D₃ s L A₂ A₃ ≫ mate D₁ D₂ r L A₁ A₂)
